title: Reactive motion control for human-robot tactile interaction
bibliography: T. Wosch and W. Feiten, ICRA 2002, pp. 3807–3812.
read_scope: Citation identity checked against DBLP; a ResearchGate-hosted abstract was found, but no primary full text or primary abstract was successfully retrieved. The secondary abstract is not used as implementation evidence.
finding: The bibliographic record establishes tactile interaction control as a research subject by 2002; no equation, response rate or robustness result is verified here.
limitation: The controller's assumptions, saturation handling and experimental limits cannot be audited from the accessed material.
plan_action: Retain as historical related work only. Implement our contact-to-response state machine from explicitly specified requirements and better-accessed sources [63,64,82], not this inaccessible paper.
novelty: Do not claim invention of tactile robot interaction; this record is evidence of earlier work, not a legal assessment of claims.

title: Real-time collision avoidance in teleoperated whole-sensitive robot arm manipulators
bibliography: V. J. Lumelsky and E. Cheung, IEEE Transactions on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics 23(1), 1993, pp. 194–203.
read_scope: NASA repository abstract and metadata. Author-hosted TR91.pdf was identified as an earlier technical report, not silently treated as the exact 1993 journal article.
finding: The abstract describes combining operator commands with whole-arm sensing for reactive obstacle avoidance in teleoperation.
limitation: The original proof conditions, sensor range and timing are not available in the abstract. Contact-only resistive film cannot supply pre-contact distance.
plan_action: Document pre-contact detection as an external robot capability. Bench demonstrations may report contact detection and subsequent response; they must not label the film a collision-prevention sensor.
novelty: Whole-arm awareness and reactive avoidance have substantial prior art.

title: Whole-arm reactive collision avoidance control of kinematically redundant manipulators
bibliography: C. L. Boddy and J. D. Taylor, ICRA 1993, vol. 3, pp. 382–387.
read_scope: DBLP identity and secondary Science Explorer abstract located. No author/publisher full text retrieved; secondary abstract is excluded as technical proof.
finding: Citation confirms an early whole-arm reactive-control contribution. Its mathematical or experimental guarantees were not verified.
limitation: Insufficient evidence to reproduce the controller or infer performance on the proposed robot.
plan_action: Our design must explicitly handle infeasible withdrawal: abort the application task and request the platform's validated stop/hold rather than promise a retreat direction for every contact configuration.
novelty: Redundancy-based whole-arm reaction is not a day-one novelty claim.

title: Programming by touch: The different way of human-robot interaction
bibliography: G. Grunwald, G. Schreiber, A. Albu-Schaffer and G. Hirzinger, IEEE Transactions on Industrial Electronics 50(4), 2003, pp. 659–666.
read_scope: DLR publication record; repository explicitly does not supply the full text. No algorithm inferred from the title.
finding: Bibliographic prior art for programming robots by physical interaction.
limitation: No controller parameters, sensor specifications or validation details were inspected.
plan_action: Treat teaching as an explicit operator-enabled mode. Record start, stop, allowed body zones and sampled robot trajectory independently from autonomous operation. Cite this paper only for historical positioning until its original text is available.
novelty: Touch teaching itself is established prior art.

title: Manual guidance for industrial robot programming
bibliography: D. Massa, M. Callegari and C. Cristalli, Industrial Robot 42(5), 2015, pp. 457–465; DOI 10.1108/IR-11-2014-0413.
read_scope: University repository metadata and complete abstract; no attached full text available.
finding: The abstract describes manual robot programming using a force/torque sensor and demonstrates an industrial application.
limitation: Force/torque sensing is not equivalent to an uncalibrated normal-contact film. Exact control gains, task constraints and failure behavior remain unverified.
plan_action: Measure teaching time, operator interventions and replay error in a controlled benchmark. Use the robot's supported hand-guiding function when available; do not substitute skin intensity for a specified six-axis sensor.
novelty: The contribution must be reduced installed sensing/maintenance cost, not manual guidance as a new application.

title: Learning inverse dynamics models with contacts
bibliography: R. Calandra, S. Ivaldi, M. P. Deisenroth, E. Rueckert and J. Peters, ICRA 2015, pp. 3186–3191; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2015.7139638.
read_scope: Author PDF, 6 pages; abstract, §§II–III, §IV-A through E and conclusion read. Filename says 2016; bibliographic paper is 2015.
finding: Mixtures of Gaussian-process contact experts predict torque residuals. In §III-A, tactile data select contacts; proximal force/torque readings supply force information. Experiments use additional calibrated joint-torque sensors as targets. The multiple-contact experiment is sequential contact at alternate obstacles.
limitation: This does not establish torque learning from the proposed film alone or arbitrary simultaneous-contact generalization. Ground-truth sensor calibration and training coverage matter.
plan_action: Keep learned dynamics outside the first control path. An optional offline comparison must log synchronized encoders, skin, reference F/T and torque targets, and split training/test by physical trial and unseen pose/contact condition.
novelty: Learning contact dynamics from skin is prior art; a new contribution needs a fair independent benchmark.

title: Realizing whole-body tactile interactions with a self-organizing, multi-modal artificial skin on a humanoid robot
bibliography: P. Mittendorfer, E. Yoshida and G. Cheng, Advanced Robotics 29(1), 2015, pp. 51–67; DOI 10.1080/01691864.2014.952493.
read_scope: Author PDF, 17 pages; hardware tables, §§3–4.3, §5, grasping experiments and limitations/conclusion examined. Equations for activity and sensory-motor mapping checked.
finding: The calibration assumptions include a fixed reference, rigid links, actuated revolute joints and accelerometer-equipped cells on body parts. Gravity-aligned motion can hide activity; complementary orientations help. HRP-2 uses balance/foot tasks above tactile upper-body behavior, with designated contact zones.
limitation: Closed-loop/underactuated structures are outside its stated calibration assumptions. The base low-cost patch lacks the required accelerometers and proximity channel. Incomplete skin coverage can leave forces unobserved.
plan_action: Use versioned CAD/manual cell-to-link positions and normals first. A removable IMU jig must have its own repeatability tests; do not advertise automatic arbitrary-sheet reconstruction. Mark coverage gaps and allowed interaction zones explicitly.
novelty: Multimodal whole-body tactile behavior and self-organization are established; low-cost serviceable implementation must be differentiated experimentally.

title: From multi-modal tactile signals to a compliant control
bibliography: E. Dean-Leon, F. Bergner, K. Ramirez-Amaro and G. Cheng, Humanoids 2016, pp. 892–898.
read_scope: Author PDF, 7 pages; §§II–III, IV-A and IV-D–F, experimental section and conclusion read.
finding: Skin signals become weighted normal virtual forces, then Jacobian-transpose joint commands. The torque resolver includes virtual nonlinear dynamics initialized from measured robot state and inner velocity feedback to limit virtual/real drift. Dynamic-model construction is parametric, not identification of actual masses from geometry alone.
limitation: The paper is not a complete deployable controller for an unspecified actuator. Gains, physical/model parameters, tracking behavior, saturation and transport delay still require platform-specific validation.
plan_action: Specify command units and robot API explicitly. Never scale torque directly into a position increment. Use an OEM-supported compliance/admittance interface or a separately tested bounded trajectory generator with state feedback, tracking-error limits and reset rules.
novelty: A general tactile-to-compliance framework is prior art.

title: Whole-body active compliance control for humanoid robots with robot skin
bibliography: E. Dean-Leon, J. R. Guadarrama-Olvera, F. Bergner and G. Cheng, ICRA 2019, pp. 5404–5410; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2019.8793258.
read_scope: TUM author-affiliated abstract and metadata; original full paper unavailable. Cheng 2019's summary is secondary evidence, not a substitute full-text read.
finding: The abstract describes hierarchical whole-body compliance on a position-controlled humanoid with more than 1,260 skin cells.
limitation: The abstract cannot establish reproducible balance constraints, gains, fault response or equivalence with our slower, less multimodal hardware.
plan_action: Keep the humanoid's existing balance/stance controller authoritative. Demonstrate the skin on a fixed-base fixture before limb integration; expose contact observations to the OEM whole-body controller rather than directly commanding leg withdrawal.
novelty: Thousands of skin cells and whole-body compliance predate this venture.

title: TOMM: Tactile omnidirectional mobile manipulator
read_scope: TUM publication record and full abstract; original implementation paper not read.
finding: The described system combines two six-DOF arms, an omnidirectional wheeled base, exchangeable end effectors and multimodal skin, with integrated hardware/software/middleware.
limitation: A wheeled robot integration is not proof of stable bipedal response. Its platform cost and full integration effort cannot be inferred from the abstract.
plan_action: Separate skin subsystem BOM from robot, gateway, software integration and tooling. First integration contract must name joint-state rate, command interface, clocks, error states and OEM supervisor ownership.
novelty: Multimodal tactile mobile manipulation is an existing application class.

title: An overview of null space projections for redundant, torque-controlled robots
bibliography: A. Dietrich, C. Ott and A. Albu-Schaffer, International Journal of Robotics Research 34(11), 2015, pp. 1385–1400.
read_scope: DLR author manuscript, 17 PDF pages; §2 assumptions, consistency formulations, §4.2 actuator-limited experiment and §§5.1–5.2 discussion read.
finding: Torque projection consistency depends on the inverse/weighting choice. Successive projections are not generally a strict hierarchy beyond two tasks. A reported dynamically consistent formulation became unstable when requested torques exceeded actuator limits/bandwidth.
limitation: Full-row-rank assumptions and inertia-model errors matter. Algebraic null-space cancellation does not guarantee feasible, stable behavior after saturation or under rank changes.
plan_action: Use the existing robot constraint solver. Test conflicting three-task cases, rank loss, actuator limits and task activation/deactivation. Require bounded commands and measured violation metrics; do not declare a weighted sum or naive projector a guaranteed priority controller.
novelty: Task hierarchy mathematics is established prior art.

title: Synthesis of whole-body behaviors through hierarchical control of behavioral primitives
bibliography: L. Sentis and O. Khatib, International Journal of Humanoid Robotics 2(4), 2005, pp. 505–518.
read_scope: Author-hosted journal PDF, 14 pages; §§1–4 including equations 17–22, §5 simulated example and discussion read.
finding: Constraints, task behavior and posture are prioritized. Projected Jacobian rank indicates whether lower-priority motion remains feasible; an infeasible task can be modified or removed. The presented example is a simulated 24-DOF humanoid.
limitation: A mathematical hierarchy under model assumptions is not a certified bound on real contact forces; the physical actuator/network limitations of our robot are unspecified by this paper.
plan_action: Define ordered responsibilities: platform stability and hard limits, collision/contact policy, application trajectory, posture. Log infeasibility and stop/hold decisions. Evaluate conflict cases in simulation before authorizing bounded fixture motion.
novelty: Hierarchical combination of balance, contact and manipulation is not novel.

title: Efficient distributed torque computation for large scale robot skin
bibliography: F. Bergner, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng, IROS 2018, pp. 1593–1599; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2018.8594144.
read_scope: TUM abstract; original author PDF at mediatum/1459300 returned rate/access errors. Detailed fixed-point/poly approximation description available only through the user-supplied Cheng 2019 review.
finding: The abstract proposes moving skin torque computations to distributed electronics to reduce central computation burden.
limitation: No audited original implementation, error bound or timing budget. Reduced host computation does not remove network latency, joint-state distribution, stale data or common-mode faults.
plan_action: Benchmark host computation and same-link wrench aggregation first. Keep individual contact records for constraints. Introduce MCU-side kinematics only after profiling shows a real bottleneck and synchronization/fault tests pass.
novelty: Distributed skin torque computation has explicit prior art.

title: Tactile-based whole-body compliance with force propagation for mobile manipulators
bibliography: Q. Leboutet, E. Dean-Leon, F. Bergner and G. Cheng, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 35(2), 2019, pp. 330–342; DOI 10.1109/TRO.2018.2889261.
read_scope: TUM abstract; primary PDF mediatum/1474210 identified but access failed. Earlier conference paper [77] read separately and not represented as this journal article.
finding: The abstract describes constrained, limb-level optimization and propagation of unaccommodated interactions through a mobile robot, experimentally evaluated on a dual-arm platform.
limitation: No original full-text audit of constraint values, feasibility conditions or controller failure handling. A mobile-manipulator result does not establish walking-humanoid balance.
plan_action: Represent unaccommodated contact as explicit supervisor status. Demand solver deadline, infeasibility, actuator saturation and stop/hold behavior in the robot integration specification; no automatic propagation into biped motion in the baseline.
novelty: Force propagation and whole-body compliance are not new features.

title: Humanoid robot HRP-2
read_scope: Citation identity checked; third-party PDF mirror found but not successfully retrieved. Related AIST platform material is not substituted for the original article.
finding: Establishes the identity of the humanoid platform used in later skin demonstrations; no original platform design data are used here.
limitation: This bibliography entry does not provide our robot's actuator, balance, thermal or payload specification.
plan_action: Require a platform-specific integration sheet, including allowable added mass/inertia by link and supervisor behavior. The skin project must not inherit HRP-2 capability or reconstruct the humanoid from this citation.
novelty: Platform provenance only; no skin novelty inferred.

title: Integration of robotic technologies for rapidly deployable robots
bibliography: E. Dean-Leon et al., IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics 14(4), 2018, pp. 1691–1700; DOI 10.1109/TII.2017.2766096.
read_scope: Author PDF contains duplicated proof material (22 pages for an approximately 11-page manuscript); architecture, §V deployment/application results, footnote 13 and conclusion read.
finding: The work integrates skin, controls and teaching. It reports installation/calibration of skin on two industrial robots in about five hours. Its functional-safety discussion explicitly identifies a starting point and preliminary productization work.
limitation: Installation time is setup-specific, not a promised production takt time. This article does not certify the proposed skin or establish its commercial cost.
plan_action: Time assembly, programming, calibration, fitting, remapping and replacement separately. Include integration/service labor in cost comparisons and publish failed/reworked units, not only successful demonstrations.
novelty: Rapid deployment is already a research objective; prove a measurable service-time advantage under matched coverage and function.

title: A survey of unknown object grasping and our fast grasping algorithm—C shape grasping
bibliography: Q. Lei, J. Meijer and M. Wisse, ICCAR 2017, pp. 150–157; DOI 10.1109/ICCAR.2017.7942677.
read_scope: TU Delft original conference repository abstract and metadata. Related thesis chapter located but not used as a complete read of the conference paper.
finding: The abstract surveys unknown-object grasp methods and describes C-shape grasp selection from partial point clouds, evaluated in simulation.
limitation: This is a grasp-planning contribution, not an affordable limb-skin fabrication or calibrated-force result.
plan_action: Out of scope for the arm/leg skin prototype. Keep grasp planner and hand sensing as external systems; do not add finger hardware, camera cost or grasp-success claims to the baseline skin deliverable.
novelty: Unknown-object grasp planning and tactile-informed grasping both have extensive prior art.

title: A unified approach for motion and force control of robot manipulators: The operational space formulation
bibliography: O. Khatib, IEEE Journal on Robotics and Automation RA-3(1), 1987, pp. 43–53; DOI 10.1109/JRA.1987.1087068.
read_scope: Author-hosted first-page abstract/introduction indexed by search; direct PDF fetch repeatedly timed out. Full equation audit uses [64,68] and the supplied Cheng 2019 text instead.
finding: The abstract introduces a task-space dynamic framework for unified motion and force control.
limitation: No additional theorem or exact implementation parameter is asserted from this limited read. A Jacobian-transpose mapping is only meaningful with compatible origins, frames and units.
plan_action: Unit-test virtual work: f dot (Jv qdot) equals (Jv transpose f) dot qdot. Check moment-origin transformations and distinguish applied environmental wrench from selected reaction command sign.
novelty: Operational-space force-to-torque mapping is foundational prior art.

title: Robot Control: The Task Function Approach
bibliography: C. Samson, B. Espiau and M. Le Borgne, Clarendon/Oxford University Press, 1991; ISBN 9780198538059.
read_scope: Bibliographic book metadata; no chapter text retrieved or read.
finding: Background reference identity only. No chapter-specific technical claim is made.
limitation: The book cannot be treated as an implementation manual actually inspected in this review.
plan_action: For each implemented task, define coordinates, error, Jacobian, units, command interface, constraints and termination conditions directly in the project specification; support implemented formulas with the accessible papers.
novelty: Task-based robot control is mature background, not a new skin contribution.

title: Integration of reactive, torque-based self-collision avoidance into a task hierarchy
bibliography: A. Dietrich, T. Wimbock, A. Albu-Schaffer and G. Hirzinger, IEEE Transactions on Robotics 28(6), 2012, pp. 1278–1293; DOI 10.1109/TRO.2012.2208667.
read_scope: DLR author manuscript, 15 PDF pages; formulation, damping/task-transition treatment, experiment setup and limitations examined.
finding: The method combines repulsive collision tasks with damping and smooth task activation to control torque discontinuities. Experiments use a fast torque-controlled platform; reported controller cycle is 1 ms.
limitation: Geometric closest-point changes and interacting repulsive fields complicate behavior. Its actuator interface and timing differ from our 100 Hz skin acquisition.
plan_action: Inflate collision geometry by the assembled skin and cable envelope. Test contact enter/leave, changing nearest points and simultaneous contacts; bound command slope and record saturation. Do not equate sample rate with full control bandwidth.
novelty: Reactive collision avoidance with smooth hierarchy integration is prior art.

title: Tactile-based compliance with hierarchical force propagation for omnidirectional mobile manipulators
bibliography: Q. Leboutet, E. Dean-Leon and G. Cheng, Humanoids 2016, pp. 926–931; DOI 10.1109/HUMANOIDS.2016.7803383.
read_scope: Author PDF, 6 pages; introduction and §II modeling assumptions, skin-force and propagation formulation read; not a complete experimental replication audit.
finding: The modeled mobile base is holonomic with planar translation and yaw. The assumptions explicitly neglect base tilting/instability and upper-limb coupling.
limitation: Those omissions are material for humanoid balance and loaded arm interaction. They cannot be carried silently into a biped product.
plan_action: Use a fixed base for the proof of concept. Return unresolved contact status to an existing platform supervisor; disable autonomous base/leg response unless a separate model and balance-validation campaign covers it.
novelty: Hierarchical propagation of skin interactions is existing research; a cheaper substrate does not supply the omitted dynamics.

title: Safe and dependable physical human-robot interaction in anthropic domains: State of the art and challenges
bibliography: R. Alami et al., IROS 2006; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2006.6936985.
read_scope: Author-hosted workshop manuscript, 15 PDF pages; §§II-A, III-A/B and IV sensor/dependability discussion read. Version/pagination differ from publisher metadata; standards discussion is historical, not current compliance advice.
finding: The paper treats physical design, sensing, control, fault handling and maintenance as coupled dependability concerns. A soft cover does not remove the consequences of high effective inertia.
limitation: Its 2006 standards and injury-limit discussion are not present-day design limits. The paper supplies no safety qualification of this new film or electronics.
plan_action: Inject open, short, stale data, reboot and wrong-map faults in the complete application chain. Verify that operator-visible coverage validity and platform stop/hold state reflect them. Test on an instrumented fixture before human contact experiments.
novelty: Mechanics-plus-control dependability is established engineering, not a differentiator by itself.

title: Impedance control: An approach to manipulation: Part III—Applications
bibliography: N. Hogan, Journal of Dynamic Systems, Measurement, and Control 107(1), 1985, pp. 17–24.
read_scope: MIT-hosted original paper, 8 pages; introduction, impedance selection and obstacle-avoidance derivation read, especially pp. 17–20 and simplifying assumptions.
finding: Interaction control specifies a dynamic relationship between motion and force. The illustrative optimization trades interface force against motion error under explicit simplified environmental assumptions.
limitation: An illustrative continuous-time optimum does not fix robust digital gains for unknown contact stiffness, transport delay, actuator bandwidth or the nonlinear resistive skin.
plan_action: Validate the complete sampled robot/controller/environment loop. Sweep fixture stiffness, delays and load classes; measure oscillation, peak reference force and settling. Do not claim passivity from positive damping alone or compute physical contact power from intensity units.
novelty: Impedance/admittance behavior is mature prior art.

title: A new actuation approach for human friendly robot design
bibliography: M. Zinn, B. Roth, O. Khatib and J. K. Salisbury, International Journal of Robotics Research 23(4–5), 2004, pp. 379–398; DOI 10.1177/0278364904042193.
read_scope: Author-hosted journal abstract/first page and one search-indexed §3.1.3 passage on saturation inspected. Direct full PDF fetch failed. Closely titled ISER/ICRA versions are not substituted.
finding: The abstract motivates reducing effective impedance while preserving torque performance. The inspected saturation passage explains loss of ideal torque-source behavior when the smaller actuator saturates.
limitation: No complete actuation-design or experimental audit; paper-specific performance cannot be assigned to our robot or skin.
plan_action: Include reflected inertia, drive friction, limits and braking behavior in the integration contract. Compare added skin/harness mass by link and resulting inertia, not just total grams saved.
novelty: Low effective impedance and lightweight actuation are prior art outside this skin subsystem.

title: Control of generalized contact motion and force in physical human-robot interaction
bibliography: E. Magrini, F. Flacco and A. De Luca, ICRA 2015, pp. 2298–2304; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2015.7139504.
read_scope: Author-hosted abstract/introduction and search-indexed early modeling passages inspected; repeated direct PDF fetches timed out. Classified conservatively because full paper was not retrieved.
finding: The inspected text treats contact-point motion/force control using robot dynamics and contact geometry. A contact on an intermediate link has a different Jacobian from the end effector.
limitation: No full experimental/equation audit. Normal-only resistive sensing cannot recover arbitrary shear or six-axis wrench, and not every desired contact motion is mechanically realizable.
plan_action: Store each taxel's rigid link, local position and unit normal. Construct its link-specific Jacobian; test zero influence of downstream joints. Keep vector force reconstruction outside the baseline specification.
novelty: Generalized contact control is prior art; no new control theorem is claimed.

title: Human-robot coexistence and contact handling with redundant robots
bibliography: E. Magrini and A. De Luca, IROS 2017, pp. 4611–4617; DOI 10.1109/IROS.2017.8206331.
read_scope: Author PDF, 7 pages; introduction, §III including Remark 1, §IV handling logic and transition description read.
finding: The method changes task behavior across contact-intensity thresholds and interpolates velocity during task abort to reduce jerk. Remark 1 specifies a single-contact algorithm in the reported formulation.
limitation: An extension discussion is not experimental proof for arbitrary simultaneous contacts. Gradual stopping trades reduced jerk against additional motion/time.
plan_action: Use explicit MONITOR, CONTACT, CONTROLLED_HOLD and FAULT states with hysteresis and latched recovery. Opposing/multiple contacts or infeasible relief request OEM hold rather than ambiguous automatic withdrawal. Test both contact onset and release.
novelty: Contact-aware task relaxation/abort is established; robustness and cost evidence are the potential contribution.

title: Human body part multicontact recognition and detection methodology
bibliography: K. S. Kim and L. Sentis, ICRA 2017, pp. 1908–1915; DOI 10.1109/ICRA.2017.7989222.
read_scope: UT Austin author-hosted abstract/introduction via search index. Direct PDF fetch failed; author-uploaded secondary full text found but not substituted for a verified full read.
finding: The system combines a 3D time-of-flight scanner with wheel-drivetrain torque sensing to associate contacts with body parts and classify predetermined interaction gestures.
limitation: This is sensor fusion with a restricted gesture vocabulary, not proof that normal touch intensity alone reveals arbitrary human intent or body part.
plan_action: Expose contact facts separately from application intent. Deliberate teaching/interaction requires explicit enable and allowed zones; any later gesture model must publish confusion matrices including accidental-contact negatives.
novelty: Multimodal touch-gesture interpretation is existing research.

title: Long-term training with a brain-machine interface-based gait protocol induces partial neurological recovery in paraplegic patients
bibliography: A. R. C. Donati et al., Scientific Reports 6, 30383, 2016; DOI 10.1038/srep30383.
read_scope: Publisher-indexed abstract and bibliographic identity; publisher full text redirected to an inaccessible identity service and PMC4980986 returned a browser challenge. No methods-section audit claimed.
finding: The abstract reports outcomes in eight participants after a year of a combined brain-machine-interface gait-training protocol incorporating multiple feedback/training components.
limitation: The abstract does not isolate electronic skin's causal contribution. It does not establish clinical benefit of this proposed skin, nor authorize extrapolation to rehabilitation products.
plan_action: Keep medical/rehabilitation claims outside the proof-of-concept article and commercial baseline. Sensory feedback may be mentioned as a distinct future application requiring its own clinical evidence and development program.
novelty: Bio-inspired sensory feedback is prior art; this project is initially a robot perception product.
